touches.text: A device talks to other devices only over the bus, never by importing them.
The exceptions are client tools a device publishes:

Scratch bus: a proof needs a bus it controls (a real store, stub devices, nobody live listening), so the cairn device publishes scratch_bus, the way db_domain's client carries scratch(). Akien 2026-11-12, answering Q#86 (8 proof imports of the bus machine in tester, codemother and librarian, measured 2026-11-11): "works for me". 2.3.8Every device has the panes the base shim defines (17.1.3.5.2), drawn by the web server (15):

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).
Owns the inspectors and gates (9.4): everything in the code pipeline that checks. The exception is diagnostic_inspector, which is base's (17.1).

Once build_inspector moves into CodeMother, code outside her reaches it over the bus: the 18 crossing calls in transitions.py, the other code sites and the 82 proofs that run a sieve over themselves. No published client tool, no fifth exception. Akien 2026-11-13, on Q#88: "over the bus. that's what it's for?"
The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict.

Where a tool lives: the general collection, cairn/tools/, is the default. A tool goes with its holder (cairn/devices/<d>/tools/) only when nothing else could ever use it: "if i build a tool for adjusting the farfignator on a vw golf from the 80s, and nothing else in the universe has a farfignator, then it can go with the car." If there is any chance somebody else might want it, it goes in the general collection.
